newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Supermarket debt takes hit.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Supermarket debt takes hit.

text.p: Supermarket junk bonds were the focus in the corporate secondary market in otherwise typically quiet Monday dealings, players said.
Penn Traffic Co debt weakend following news of a drop in first quarter revenues, traders said.
"Penn 9-5/8 paper fell two points to trade at 52-1/4 bid, 53 offer," one high-yield trader said.
The supermarket reported an 8.3 percent decline in its first quarter revenues of $759.4 million compared to $827.7 million a year ago.
The company said same store sales were off 8.1 percent for the 13 weeks ended May 3 versus the same period last year.

Among other Penn Traffic issues, the company's 8.625 percent notes were quoted off one point at 81 bid, 82 offer, while the supermarket's 10-1/4, 10-3/8 and 11-1/2 percent paper traded off 1/2 point, traders said.
Meanwhile, Grand Union Co debt fell 1-1/2 points continuing a volatile trading session begun last week.
"Trading continues to be volatile ... the 12-percent notes traded as high as 80 bid at the open but later came off to trade at 77-1/2 bid," another high-yield trader said.
The food retailer's debt fell from the high eighties last week after dissappointing earnings and news of a corporate restructruring, hit the market, players said.
The company's debt ratings were later downgraded by two credit agencies.
In the broader high-yield market, prices ended the day unchanged to 1/8 higher in modest trading activity, players said.
"Earlier we were a bit lower but prices reversed to end the day about an 1/8 or so higher, " said one player. "But, baiscally it's been a quiet day."
In other news, Reeves Industries debt dropped 1-1/2 points on Monday extending its decline to eight points since last week, traders said.
The 11 percent senior notes due 2002 ended the day weaker at 75 bid, 77 offer, traders said.

Players said the company has been plagued by unconfirmed rumors it had to borrow money to cover debt interest and operations. Further talk that its Chief Financial Officer resigned exacerbated the debt's performance, they said.
"For a company who had been cash flow positive and all of a sudden had to borrow $20 million ahead of a coupon payment in July is cause for concern," said one market source.
Reeves Industries could not be reached for comment.
Recently, Moody's cut the textiles manufacturer's debt to Caa from B3, keeping a negative outlook on the rating.
Moody's said the actions reflected the continued weakness of the company's earnings and uncertainty regarding timing and realizable value from the intended sale of all, or parts of the company.

Turning to primary sector for high-yield issues, Viasystems Inc sold $400 million in 10-year 144A notes to yield a spread of 310 basis points over Treasuries, a syndicate source said. The issue was oversubsribed and upsized by $100 million, the source added.
In the high-grade secondary arena, spreads to U.S. Treasuries remained unchanged in a trading session deemed as very subdued by market players.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond closed up 3/32 at 96-17/32 to yield 6.90 percent.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
